callers.source: read.c:3259-3269; creation assigns the replacement species before the wizard force prompt and consumes the returned mtype.
trap.c:746-754; statue revival uses cant_revive() before selecting saved traits or a fresh replacement.
zap.c:982-994; figurine conversion consumes the possible species substitution before makemon().

functions.name: create_particular_parse
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:3137-3251 in full. Preserved the initial quantity from gm.multi, digit-by-digit count consumption, QUAN_LIMIT and monster_census(FALSE) fallback, the source ordered case-insensitive gear/state/gender searches with in-place blanking, mungspaces(), disposition prefixes, wizard-only * and random handling, name_to_mon() gender output, explicit gender conflict, and the name_to_monclass() concrete, invisible, worm-tail, class, and failure arms. The returned request is local data; its inputs include the hero role, command count, wizard flag, source census and initialized monster catalog. No random draw, message, or game-state mutation occurs. Supporting minion.c monster_census40–57 is pure: it traverses the live monster list, excludes dead monsters and guards with mx zero, and applies canonical canspotmon only for a spotted census. The source-pinned test covers these filters, including the default sensing predicate.

callers.source: read.c:3382-3388; each getlin() answer is munged and passed to create_particular_parse() before creation or the retry diagnostics.

functions.name: create_particular_creation
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:3252-3371 in full. Preserved the non-random firstchoice and cant_revive replacement before the y_n force prompt, then source ordered mkclass()/rndmonst() selection, explicit gender conflict and MM_NOEXCLAM/MM_MINVIS flags, makemon() return and retry behavior, tamedog/set_malign disposition arms, saddle creation after can_saddle/which_armor, hidden tests for M1_HIDE, M1_CONCEAL plus OBJ_AT, and eel plus is_pool, sleeping state, flash_mon() and final newcham() order. The makemon caller is awaited through its runtime continuation; its marker admits both ordinary MM_NOEXCLAM requests and the C gender-conflict arm that has only one gender bit, with optional MM_MINVIS. mon_set_minvis() remains after placement and peace_minded() as in makemon.c:1299-1301. The caller now awaits canonical mon.c flash_mon(), which completes the whole display.c flash_glyph_at() animation before creation continues. Independent hidden-trapper and invisible-newt recordings match each source animation frame, final screen, cursor and RNG sequence; the underlying temporary vision, ordinary mon_to_glyph and hero-memory background behavior is recorded with the display.c source goal.

callers.source: read.c:3405; a successful parse reaches create_particular_creation() and returns its Boolean result.

functions.name: create_particular
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:3372-3411 in full. Preserved the five-attempt countdown, Escape return, parse retry diagnostics and first retry prompt extension, then the final enough-tries message or awaited creation return. The source result is carried through both production callers; no fire-and-forget creation remains. The command seam no longer lists an obsolete monster-request refusal class because unknown text follows this source retry loop. Integration uses the canonical thats_enough_tries constant from decl.c common strings. A production-caller unit test verifies that four invalid answers retain the expanded prompt and a fifth ends the retry loop, with normal message acknowledgements between answers; it pins the source exclamation mark.

callers.source: wizcmds.c:203-210; wizard #wizgenesis clears debug_mongen, awaits create_particular(), restores the flag, and returns ECMD_OK.
makemon.c:1569-1577; the wizard create-monster scroll/wand/spell path awaits create_particular() and uses its Boolean to continue or stop prompting.

Active class/random, saddle, tame, explicit gender-conflict, force-revival, create_critters scroll/spell, and bones.c, trap.c and zap.c cant_revive families retain empty recording arrays until their own production routes are exercised. functions.name: do_screen_description
functions.sourceReview: Read nethack-c/upstream/src/pager.c:1247-1630 in full, together with add_cmap_descr():1133-1244 and append_str():82-104. The port preserves restricted-vision and swallow ordering, monster/object/misc/cmap/warning/venom passes, rotated water/lava aliases, trap and drawbridge suppression, optional overrides with source re-entry, many-things refinement, and final lookat refinement. It uses the C boulder fallback and Is_rogue_level selection, independent NOTHING/UNEXPLORED glyph checks, DEF_INVISIBLE semantics, source warning co-location text, temporary EHalluc_resistance and terrain restoration, stored-glyph pet override handling without a live-monster guard, and BUFSZ-bounded case-insensitive append_str behavior. The typed one-byte caller enters the same renderer and emits the C no-match message. Existing discarded or unported caller families remain explicitly open rather than represented by invented behavior. Canonical display.c map_glyphinfo now resolves unexplored, warning and stored monster glyph families without reading rendered cell sidecars or rerolling glyph selection. Lookup uses selected coordinates, while the encoded prefix follows windows.c decode_mixed and utf8map.c mixed_to_utf8 at (0,0). Supporting glyph resolution preserves pet override before hero handling, the independent NOOVERRIDE pet reset, nonzero hero-space overrides, the literal showsyms[pet_override] test, and Rogue monster/warning colors with the stored-map clamp before hero showrace adjustment. Literal source-pinned assertions cover ant-class fallback at ordinary and hero coordinates and zero-byte pet overrides with a customized stone symbol.

callers.source: pager.c do_look() dispatches ordinary map farlook, quick look, and typed one-character symbol lookup to do_screen_description(); the JavaScript command routes these paths through the complete renderer.
getpos.c auto_describe() requests a description for the selected displayed map cell; the JavaScript caller uses the canonical pager path.
cmd.c doclicklook() dispatches the clicked look path to the shared description behavior; JavaScript command dispatch reaches the canonical pager renderer for displayed cells.
cmd.c dolookaround() scans source-interesting stored glyphs and calls do_screen_description; JavaScript uses the same stored-glyph filter and canonical renderer.
display.c show_glyph() requests the first description after installing a glyph; startup accessibility queues this production notice through do_screen_description().
cmd.c dolookaround() describes visible interesting cells; the accessibility lookaround caller validates a displayed glyph and invokes the shared do_screen_description() path.

evidence.entryPointReview: This is the complete pager.c do_screen_description source unit, including its add_cmap_descr and append_str contracts. Production callers reviewed are pager.c do_look (ordinary, quick, and typed symbol paths), getpos.c auto_describe, cmd.c doclicklook and dolookaround, and display.c show_glyph through the startup accessibility caller. Existing sink/fountain farlook recordings exercise displayed cmap collection; independently selected typed comma recordings exercise the one-byte unknown-symbol arm and no-match output, and the typed { variation exercises the shared sink/fountain symbol branch. recordings/cmd.c/lookaround-command.session.json reaches cmd.c dolookaround and produces the room plus doorway description through the canonical path, but it is not used as a new recording here. getpos.c getpos_menu remains an active caller entry with no matching recording; displayed glyph accessibility has no independent recording; later click/queued, lootabc, swallowed, hallucination, and multichar encyclopedia branches remain explicit caller gaps. No claim is made about an unmeasured later Knight boundary. Final source review confirms that hallucinated synthetic objects retain vague names through object_from_map, real OBJ_NAME entries use mksobj rather than mkobj, strange objects omit an article, and hallucinated monster naming suppresses the invisible prefix. Stored-glyph lookaround filtering precedes all naming, including squares with hidden live objects. The added getpos helper covers only GLOC_INTERESTING and its door predicate; no broader getpos completion is claimed. The rejected 41361354 candidate exposed rendered-byte and null-cell classification regressions. The correction uses canonical glyph identity and raw tty bytes for lookup, keeping encoded-prefix coordinates distinct; source-pinned display checks cover that contract. No broader display.c file completion is claimed.

callers.source: mklev.c makelevel() selects the special proto and calls makemaz(); js/mklev.js makelevel() resolves the current special-level loader and dispatches makemaz() at lines 657-737.
mkmaze.c makemaz() resolves the protofile and calls load_special(); js/mklev.js makemaz() invokes load_special(protofile, state) and performs the level-generation tail at lines 1805-1838.
sp_lev.c load_special() loads the Lua program through the des.* table and applies post-processing; js/mklev.js load_special() invokes the registered loader and special-level API at lines 1777-1802.
The production registry imports QUEST_LEVEL_LOADERS and spreads it into SPECIAL_LEVEL_LOADERS before makelevel dispatch.

functions.name: u_can_engrave
functions.sourceReview: Read the complete engrave.c:503-541 body. The function computes SURFACE_AT first; the swallowed-animal refusal precedes the swallowed-whirly floor message, while amorphous engulfers bypass terrain checks. The non-swallowed order is lava, pool or fountain, air, then !ACCESSIBLE. It then checks cantwield before check_capacity and returns the boolean result. The JS port preserves that branch and callback order, exact messages, and uses surface_typ() for SURFACE_AT. Direct callees are the is_animal/is_whirly macros, is_lava(), is_pool(), surface(), IS_FOUNTAIN, IS_AIR, ACCESSIBLE, cant_reach_floor(), cantwield(), and check_capacity(); each is already ported and none is replaced with note_unported(). The source function can emit text and surface() can draw through hallucinated hliquid(), so it is impure. engrave.c:doengrave() checks the returned false and returns ECMD_FAIL; js/engrave.js now does the same before any prompt.

result.summary: The v5 evaluation matches 34/45 screens, then stops at segment 0 step 34 when the Ranger selects a wished cursed scroll of teleportation with `r`, `g`. functions.name: resist
functions.sourceReview: Read and compared the complete zap.c resist() definition at lines 6100-6158. The fake-player Conflict early return precedes all draws; attack level follows the exact class switch; defense level is capped at 50 or floored to the player level only for a monster player and otherwise to 1; then one rn2(100 + alev - dlev) comparison decides resistance. A resisted hit calls shieldeff_mon only when tell is true and rounds positive damage upward with (damage + 1) / 2. Damage is then subtracted, and lethal damage dispatches to monkilled(mtmp, "", AD_RBRE) only while gm.m_using is true, otherwise killed(mtmp); both calls discard their void result. The JS port preserves this order, uses the caller's RNG/environment bundle for death side effects, removes the former UnsupportedZapError refusal, and returns the resistance result. Existing killed/monkilled owners are invoked; no return-valued callee is substituted or skipped.

source.branch: In use_unicorn_horn(), obj is present and uncursed, so C skips the cursed adverse-effect branch. HBlinded has a timeout greater than u.ucreamed, the hero is not swallowed by an engulfer whose attack sustains blindness, and no other timed trouble qualifies. trouble_count is therefore one (BLINDED); no trouble shuffle is needed. With this unblessed horn, C evaluates rn2(d(2,2)), gets d(2,2)=3 and rn2(3)=2, clamps val_limit to one, and calls make_blinded(u.ucreamed, TRUE). Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:4214-4425 defines doapply(); its SADDLE arm at 4300-4302 assigns use_saddle() to res, and the common tail returns res at 4419-4424. nethack-c/upstream/src/steed.c:36-139 defines use_saddle(): it selects a direction, validates the adjacent monster and saddleability, computes chance from dexterity, charisma, tame level, role, riding skill, impairment, equipment, and BUC, wakes the steed, rolls rn2(100), and on success removes the saddle from hero inventory and calls put_saddle_on_mon(). The recorded Knight succeeds on roll 8 and the command spends a turn.

The source state contract for the successful saddle path is steed.c:133-163: the saddle leaves hero inventory; put_saddle_on_mon() attaches it to the monster inventory, sets monster misc_worn_check and saddle owornmask to W_SADDLE, sets saddle.leashmon to monster m_id, and updates monster extrinsics. js/apply.js:2293-2397 confirms the first failure: its switch omits SADDLE and its default throws UnsupportedApplyError for the selected object type. js/steed.js has no use_saddle() implementation, so wiring only a dispatch label would still leave the selected C function absent; js/dog.js currently holds can_saddle() and put_saddle_on_mon() implementations originating from steed.c.

After the first blocker, the C recording reaches #ride: step 30 selects adjacent direction u, step 31 asks “Force the mount to succeed?”, and step 32 answers y; C then shows Ride in the status line and the pony under the hero. Upstream steed.c:176-193 routes doride() through mount_steed(), whose success path at 358-382 sets u.usteed, removes the monster from its square, moves the hero with teleds(), and marks disp.botl.

The corresponding JavaScript ride path is already wired: js/extcmdlist_data.js:111 maps ride to doride, js/cmd.js:5146-5148 dispatches it, and js/steed.js:839-860 implements doride() and :204-429 implements mount_steed(). mount_steed() still refuses other source branches at js/steed.js:229, :262, :296, :308, and :322; maybewakesteed() also stops when it must wake a frozen steed at :800. The recorded healthy Knight’s forced ride of an awake, tame pony does not enter those branches. The saved evaluation stops before this path, so the recorded C behavior is reachable evidence, not yet a JavaScript parity claim.

functions.name: potionhit
functions.sourceReview: Compared the complete potion.c:potionhit() definition (1625-1928) against the port: target-is-hero and monster branches, direct saddle hit and water-on-saddle path, all potion type switches, resistance and polymorph guards, blindness duration draws and resistance ordering, anger/sleep cleanup, shop disposition, and final object consumption. Preserved evaluation and RNG order. For the hero POT_POLYMORPH arm, You_feel("a little %s") precedes the Unchanging/Antimagic polyself guard exactly as C. For monster targets, potion.c obtains distance through distu(tx,ty), whose include/hack.h definition calls dist2 and whose hacklib.c body returns dx*dx+dy*dy; JS now uses that squared distance for the distance<3 vapor test. The return from H2Opotion_dip() is consumed in the saddle-water branch, so that whole helper was also ported and its Boolean is used. potion.c calls potionbreathe() as a void callee; the active partial helper arms remain enabled, while unsupported vapor types are source-named with note_unported('potion.c potionbreathe') and skipped so potionhit continues to its shop/object-release tail. The C calls to sounds.c:Soundeffect(), potion.c:explode_oil(), zap.c:bhitm() in the monster polymorph arm, and mon.c:mcureblindness() discard their results; JS records those exact source gaps and never treats the return as data. B28 ports the upward toss path at dothrow.c:toss_up(), which calls potionhit on the hero and discards the toss_up Boolean as C does. No case or seed condition was added. B27 additionally fixes the shared no-env.random runtime path at potionhit(): the C function uses process RNG calls including rnl(), so js/potion.js imports rnl into its default random bundle rather than requiring one caller to inject it. A focused no-random-seam call and the independent melee recording exercise that default.

dothrow.c:thitmonst() (2264) calls potionhit(mon,obj,POTHIT_HERO_THROW) after the thrown potion hits a monster. The independent Wizard recording and admitted v7 range exercise this production call.

functions.name: inside_gas_cloud
functions.sourceReview: Compared the complete upstream region.c:inside_gas_cloud() body (1091-1165) in C order. It chooses mtmp or &youmonst, extends ttl by five for a fog-cloud occupant while ttl<20, then returns immediately for dam<1. The hero arm checks m_poisongas_ok first; when not blind it pluralizes the correct eye body part, prints the sting message, and calls make_blinded(1,FALSE). Without Poison_resistance it prints the burning-lungs and blood-cough messages, wakes nearby monsters, draws rnd(dam)+5, applies Maybe_Half_Phys, then the damp-towel Half_gas_damage reduction, calls losehp, clears seen poison resistance, and returns false. With Poison_resistance it only coughs, wakes nearby monsters, records seen poison resistance, and returns false. The monster arm checks m_poisongas_ok; for a non-silent monster it coughs only when cansee or distu()<8 (distu is squared Euclidean distance), then wakes nearby monsters. It next applies heros_fault/setmangry, updates mblinded/mcansee for an eyed visible monster, returns on resists_poison, or draws rnd(dam)+5 and subtracts HP. A dead monster goes to killed() for a hero-created cloud or monkilled() otherwise, and the callback returns true only when it remains dead after that void helper (the return is consumed by run_regions to remove the cached monster ID). JavaScript preserves this order and uses the existing source ports for m_poisongas_ok, body_part, makeplural, make_blinded, wake_nearto, losehp, dist2, monster_resists_element, setmangry, killed, and monkilled. The C function's direct damage RNG is exactly one rnd(dam) in the hero vulnerable branch and one rnd(dam) in the non-resistant monster branch; the strict recordings confirm ordering with each helper's draws. The preflight refusal for positive damage was removed. Existing mon.c killed()/monkilled() implementations retain explicit unsupported internal branches; when reached, the void-call adapter records note_unported('mon.c ...') for every state object and invokes any supplied unsupported hook. A focused long-worm witness confirms the named gap is recorded even with an injected state; the ordinary newt death route matches C through killed() and the callback true return. No return from note_unported is used as data.

The port preserves observe_object before artifact placement/touch, fatal touch and polymorph return paths, crysknife restoration, Fumbling and wished fatal-corpse priority, addinv_core0 before slot/burden checks, pickup_burden max, merge undo via splitobj, autoquiver, prinv/update/encumber order, then drop message, nomerge clear and floor/swallow versus hitfloor handling. functions.name: shieldeff
functions.sourceReview: Reviewed the complete display.c:shieldeff definition (1110-1126). It returns when flags.sparkle is false; when cansee(x,y) is true it loops through the complete SHIELD_COUNT shield_static[] sequence in declaration order, performing show_glyph(cmap_to_glyph(...)), flush_screen(1), and nh_delay_output() for every frame, then newsym(x,y) restores the square. result.summary: The v13 replay stops at the named GRAPPLING_HOOK refusal in js/apply.js before C reaches apply.c:use_grapple. C uses the unwielded-hook arm to wield the tool and queue a repeated doapply; its later matching source trace reaches a selected empty-object target and prints “Nothing happens.” The implementation scope is the complete grapple helper family plus doapply caller wiring, with the existing getpos, wield, targeting, and movement dependencies preserved in C order.

source.branch: For a selected GRAPPLING_HOOK, use_grapple returns without acting when swallowed. If the hook is not uwep, C calls wield_tool(obj, "cast"); on success it queues doapply and the object letter and returns ECMD_TIME. Once wielded, it prompts for a target, filters visible in-range squares, applies the weapon-skill menu/RNG branches, and resolves trap, object, monster, surface, or self targets. The selected case is a human Wizard who is not swallowed or blind: its first hook input is the unheld-tool arm, then its later target is an adjacent visible empty square and its source-selected tohit value is 1.
callers: The #apply command dispatches to apply.c:doapply; its GRAPPLING_HOOK switch arm assigns the return from use_grapple(obj) to the command result.
Within use_grapple, an unwielded hook that wield_tool accepts queues a repeated doapply and the hook inventory letter, so the next command reaches the wielded-target flow.
dependencies: wield_tool(obj, "cast") returns a Boolean consumed by the wield/queue branch.
uwep_skill_type, grapple_range, and can_grapple_location provide the weapon skill, maximum range, and target eligibility; the latter two have consumed return values.
getpos_sethilite and getpos mutate the target coordinate; use_grapple consumes getpos’s negative cancellation result.
The skilled menu consumes select_menu’s count/selection and an RNG gate; preserve C menu and random-call order.
The target branch consumes m_at’s monster pointer and enexto’s Boolean; pickup_object, attack_checks, and thitmonst effects are called with discarded return values in C.
u_wipe_engr, hurtle, spoteffects, losehp, and the target-description/display helpers preserve source side effects and command results.

Upstream makemon.c:1157-1185 records byyou from the requested coordinates and, outside level generation, invokes enexto_core before construction. The first mismatch therefore precedes worm initialization: permit this source-supported runtime named-creation path, then verify the entire relocation and tail result against C.

The later dagger action reaches dothrow.c:thitmonst and worm.c:cutworm at step 41, so cutworm is downstream of and outside this first-mismatch scope.

result.summary: This is a caller-wiring defect in the already-portable makemon.c:bagotricks() function, not missing whole-source behavior in makemon(). C bagotricks() invokes makemon(NULL, u.ux, u.uy, NO_MM_FLAGS) and receives a monster pointer or NULL after the full makemon() source tail. Frozen JS already splits the same constructor and tail: synchronous makemon() requires a runtimeContinuation, while makemon_runtime() supplies it, runs the asynchronous group/inventory/output tail, and returns the created monster or NULL. Frozen js/makemon.js already imports makemon_runtime and uses it in create_critters(); bagotricks() alone uses the synchronous API at this callsite. The assigned fix scope is therefore a divergence-fix in bagotricks(), with makemon reviewed as a dependency. This overlaps A52’s assigned makemon creation/helper work, which owns the adapter behavior.

source.branch: The assigned branch is the charged creation loop in the whole C bagotricks() function (2554-2601): after charge consumption and the rn2(23)/rnd(7) count choice, it calls makemon(NULL, u.ux, u.uy, NO_MM_FLAGS), then counts a non-NULL returned monster and whether it is visible or sensed. Frozen JS represents the rest of bagotricks() and already imports makemon_runtime, but this callsite passes its runtime shape to synchronous makemon() without an async continuation. For this call shape, no missing makemon() returned-value branch was found: the existing makemon_runtime() wraps the synchronous constructor, runs the C runtime suffix, and returns its monster or NULL. The narrow defect classification is divergence-fix in bagotricks(); makemon() remains a reviewed dependency and A52 reservation overlap.

It draws rnd(11), then visits cases 1 through 11 in order with source fallthrough, removing the first present intrinsic among fire resistance, teleportation, poison resistance, telepathy, cold resistance, invisibility, see invisible, speed, stealth, protection, or aggravate monster. result.summary: Quaffing the final lit potion of oil reaches the C peffect_oil effect before the potion is consumed. The refusal occurs at generic object deallocation: mkobj.c dealloc_obj() must stop the object's BURN_OBJECT timer, whose cleanup_burn() removes its light source and clears lamplit. The JavaScript quaff path currently reaches inventory preflight without the stopObjectTimers lifecycle hook; preflight also requires deleteObjectLightSource for a lit object. Keep this source scope on the whole dealloc_obj() cleanup branch and its caller wiring, separate from peffect_oil() and the later input boundary.

callers: shk.c obfree() directly calls mkobj.c dealloc_obj() after billing and worn-object handling.

light.c del_light_source() removes the object light; cleanup_burn() also restores unused oil age, clears lamplit, and updates carried inventory.

evidence: The assigned diagnostic artifact `.cache/synthetic-scans/v15/wizard-quaffs-lit-oil-resist.json` records a stop at step 66 with `stopObjectTimers is not available for otyp 321`; the assigned queue entry records exactly 2 remaining screens of 68. The source owner is not supplied by the queue (sourceFile is null), so the source trace below attributes the refusal.

The assigned C recording `challenges/cases/v15/wizard-quaffs-lit-oil-resist.session.json`, segment 0, steps 65-67, shows `q` opening the drink prompt, `p` quaffing the lit oil, and C step 66 recording `d(2,4)=4 @ peffect_oil(potion.c:1277)` with the message “You burn your face.” Step 67 is the separate following space input, reported by C as `Unknown command`. The effect runs before the consumption cleanup; the later input boundary is not the timer owner.

In `nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:617-640`, dodrink() calls dopotion(); dopotion() calls peffects(), then after a negative result reaches useup(). `potion.c:1411-1413` dispatches POT_OIL to peffect_oil(), and `potion.c:1262-1293` handles the lit branch (damage, slime cleanup, Wisdom exercise) without deleting the potion or stopping its timer. This separates the recorded effect RNG from the subsequent refusal.

In `nethack-c/upstream/src/invent.c:1310-1332`, useup() routes a one-item stack through useupall(), which calls shk.c obfree() at `invent.c:1316`. `shk.c:1187-1274` finishes ordinary object cleanup by calling dealloc_obj().

The complete C owner is `nethack-c/upstream/src/mkobj.c:2745-2795`, dealloc_obj(): after validating a detached object, it calls obj_stop_timers() when obj->timed is nonzero (`2765-2767`), then handles any remaining light source (`2777-2780`) before releasing the object. This is the whole-function scope for the source-owned cleanup branch.

`nethack-c/upstream/src/timeout.c:1727-1789` gives POT_OIL a BURN_OBJECT timer when lit. The timeout table maps BURN_OBJECT to cleanup_burn() at `1984`; obj_stop_timers() walks matching object timers, invokes each registered cleanup, then sets obj->timed to zero (`2373-2397`). cleanup_burn() removes the light, restores the unused fuel time, clears lamplit, and refreshes carried inventory (`1824-1844`).

At the examined JavaScript commit, `js/potion.js:1805-1830` ends dopotion() with useup(otmp) without lifecycle hooks. `js/invent.js:3675-3685` preflights stopObjectTimers first and deleteObjectLightSource for a lit object; `js/obj.js:1143-1162` consumes those same hooks in dealloc_obj(). `js/timeout.js:1187-1220` already implements obj_stop_timers() and the BURN_OBJECT cleanup, so the first refusal is missing lifecycle wiring into the existing timer cleanup, not missing peffect_oil() behavior.

result.summary: The remaining screen is blocked by js/cmd.js rhack() rejecting a count-prefixed nonmovement command before it dispatches the already implemented pickup path. C parse() sets command_count=5 and gm.multi=4, but the comma binding reaches hack.c:dopickup(), which copies command_count and immediately sets gm.multi=0 before calling pickup(-count). This is one counted pickup, not an automatic repeat. The actionable scope is a divergence fix to the cmd.c:rhack() count gate; the saved queue annotation naming parse()/moveloop_core() as the refusal owner is too broad.

source.branch: For a count-prefixed comma command on a reachable floor square with one five-dagger stack, cmd.c:parse() leaves gc.command_count=5 and gm.multi=4. The comma row at cmd.c:1799 binds to dopickup; cmd.c:rhack() calls the bound function without a count-specific refusal. hack.c:dopickup() copies gc.command_count, sets gm.multi=0, and calls pickup(-count), so this handler consumes the count as the requested item quantity and prevents moveloop_core() from repeating it. In js/cmd.js, the generic state.multi > 0 nonmovement guard rejects the command before runPickupCommand() reaches js/hack.js:dopickup() and js/pickup.js:pickup(). The mismatch is an overbroad refusal in an implemented command path, not a missing pickup selection function.

Upstream cmd.c:parse() at 5096-5149 sets gc.command_count from the 5 prefix and then sets gm.multi to 4. Upstream cmd.c:rhack() at 3627-3843 resolves the comma binding and calls its function at 3724-3748 without rejecting a positive gm.multi. The command table at 1799 binds comma to dopickup.

The code comment at js/hack.js:4351-4352 documents why the guard currently blocks larger counts.

The source patch series is limited to deterministic runtime, stable sorting, RNG logging, and terminal capture according to nethack-c/patches/README.md; searching nethack-c/patches for cmd.c, hack.c, pickup.c, and allmain.c finds no edits to these gameplay functions. For each in range it calls resist(mtmp, TOOL_CLASS, 0, NOTELL); if the consumed Boolean result is false, or the monster is a shopkeeper, it calls tamedog(mtmp, NULL, TRUE) and discards that return. In this recording, the level-1 hero’s magic harp gives distance 1 and the adjacent orc is at squared distance 1. functions.name: doname_base
functions.sourceReview: Compared the complete objnam.c:doname_base (1223-1751), preserving xname-before-identification order; quantity/article and fake-artifact handling; BUC, empty/trapped/locked/greased state; worn suffixes and body-part wording; the full object-class switch; charges, candle timer adjustment, corpse/egg names, quiver and wizard-gender suffixes; unpaid, live-price and remembered-price branches; wizard weight; and sequential BUFSZ truncation. Removed selected preflightDoname refusals for the valid source branches. The C-discarded impossible leash branch remains note_unported('pline.c impossible'); apply.c:snuff_candle remains a separate gap. This correction also rechecked the C Concat and ConcatF1/F2 macros: every sequential append is bounded by the remaining BUFSZ body bytes, Concat uses strncat(spaceleft + delta), ConcatF uses snprintf(spaceleft + delta), delta-one writes back over the actual clipped final byte, and wizard weight is appended before strprepend. The consumed objnam.c:xname_flags gameover disclosure branch now uses the existing read.js text helpers in C order; objnam.c:distant_name saves, zeros and restores o_id in C order. These are supporting corrections with no separate whole-function credit. The result updates object identification and price-quote extrema, so this function is impure. Required return-valued helpers were also compared at their complete source definitions and tested: shk.c:get_cost_of_shop_item (2809-2843), get_pricing_units (2846-2859), oid_price_adjustment (2864-2872), get_cost (2877-2988), contained_cost (2995-3042), unpaid_cost (3260-3305), corpsenm_price_adj (4275-4316), and getprice (4319-4358). Their original C caller order remains in the naming path; C-discarded impossible diagnostics stay explicitly named at the relevant helper boundaries. invent.c:count_contents and timeout.c:peek_timer are reused as the existing canonical helpers. The final pointer-offset pass preserves C xname_flags returning buf+4 after stripping the article, then doname_base stripping the poisoned prefix with bp += 9 while leaving bp_eos and bpspaceleft unchanged; those byte offsets remain in force for every later bounded append. The corpse_xname result stays in prefix[] while bp retains xname() body text, and known egg species similarly stays in prefix while only the bounded laid-by-you text appends to bp. Source-pinned tests fill the body to C limits for poisoned and article-bearing names, and verify corpse gender and egg suffixes fit only when their prefixes stay outside bp. The selected object-naming-preflight contract cleanup removes assertObjectNameable and its no-op call sites from pickup.js and invent.js, retaining actual priced-object checks. Supporting shk.c:append_price_quote (454-493) now uses UTF-8 byte lengths for both its suffix and input buffer, matching C’s strict `len2 < BUFSZ - len - 1` guard. Its caller appends the returned suffix and advances the body end while preserving C’s unchanged cached bpspaceleft; wizard weight therefore uses pre-quote remaining bytes. The get_cost_of_shop_item caller also matches C’s current-shop/coin/ball/chain checks before get_obj_location and its get_cost-before-get_pricing_units call order; source-pinned proxy tests verify those orders.

C branch semantics: water_prayer(TRUE) scans the floor objects at the hero square; for an eligible POT_WATER it sets blessed=TRUE, cursed=FALSE, and bknown according to visibility. With changed water and an unblind hero it prints the altar potion glow. The saved recording shows exactly “The potion on the altar glows light blue for a moment.--More--”.

Recorded continuation: challenges/cases/v17/prayer-coaligned-neutral-water-prayer-glow-pager-continuation.session.json step 53 has key y and the prayer completion light/finish message followed by --More--; step 54 key space records the water-prayer glow line. This verifies the title’s pager continuation reaches the visible source effect.

Saved evaluation: challenges/evaluations/20261001190602-v17.json reports 54/55 screens matched and one remaining screen. At step 54 the first differing cell is C “T” versus JS “Y”, and cursor positions are C [62,0,1] versus JS [27,4,1]. The diagnostic .cache/synthetic-scans/v17/prayer-coaligned-neutral-water-prayer-glow-pager-continuation.json identifies the same boundary and records note_unported gaps pray_revive and water_prayer.

JavaScript source: js/pray.js:1469-1516 implements prayer_done(); its p_type-3 altar branch records note_unported("pray.c water_prayer") at line 1514 then immediately invokes pleased(). pleased() at js/pray.js:1727 prints a first message beginning “You feel…”, matching the diagnostic’s JS Y cell. The missing water_prayer output, not the page renderer, is the first cause.

The helper returns whether it changed water. C discards the return for p_type 0, 1, and 3, but consumes it in p_type 2 at pray.c:2327 to choose penalties versus pleased(). Keep this consumed-return dependency explicit if the caller’s unsupported p_type-2 branch is included in the implementation task.

goals.detail: Root compared whole wizard.c:aggravate and nine existing callers against C. Hero tower membership is cached, dead/other-region monsters skipped in fmon order, exact wait/appear bits cleared, sleeping cleared, conditional rn2(5) only on immobile monsters and zero-roll thaw preserved. Existing In_W_tower return dependency is source checked. Exact callers are peffect_invisibility, cursed_book, m_respond_shrieker, m_respond, doturn, dosit throne case11, domonnoise MS_SHRIEK, domonability shriek, mcast_spell MCAST_AGGRAVATION. result.summary: The first screen/RNG mismatch occurs on the monster turn after a cursed invisibility potion. potion.c peffect_invisibility() calls the void wizard.c aggravate(); JavaScript currently records note_unported() there, leaving the sleeping orc asleep. Port the whole aggravate() function and wire its existing JavaScript gap callers. The queue’s distfleeck RNG tag is downstream of the missing state change.

source.branch: For each living monster in the current fmon chain whose In_W_tower() result matches the hero’s, aggravate() clears STRAT_WAITFORU and STRAT_APPEARMSG and sets msleeping to zero. If that monster cannot move, it then rolls rn2(5); only a zero result clears mfrozen and restores mcanmove. The function returns void and emits no message.
callers: Recorded path: cmd.c binds quaff to potion.c dodrink() -> dopotion() -> peffects() -> peffect_invisibility() (:811-837); for a cursed potion, peffect_invisibility() emits the known-presence message and calls aggravate() at :832. JavaScript routes q through js/cmd.js dodrink dispatch into js/potion.js dodrink()/dopotion()/peffects()/peffect_invisibility(); peffect_invisibility() currently leaves note_unported('wizard.c aggravate') at js/potion.js:1385.
spell.c cursed_book() calls aggravate() in cursed-book result case 1 at :141-144; js/spell.js cursed_book() records the same named gap at :306 when operating on the live game state.

mon.c m_respond_shrieker() calls aggravate() after its shriek and any summon at :4089-4105, and m_respond() calls it for a hostile visible Erinys at :4122-4130. js/mon.js has named gaps at :3645 and :3674.
pray.c dopray() calls aggravate() when the deity ignores the petitioner (:2441-2448) and when prayer is attempted in Gehennom (:2450-2456); js/pray.js records named gaps at :1681 and :1693.
sit.c dosit() calls aggravate() on the negative-luck case (:185-193); js/sit.js records a named gap at :468.
sounds.c growl() calls aggravate() for MS_SHRIEK (:960-964); js/sounds.js growl() records a named gap at :1199.

cmd.c domonability() calls aggravate() when the hero form shrieks and is not buried (:932-937); js/cmd.js still refuses its shrieker branch with UnsupportedHeroCommandBranchBoundaryError at :3589-3592.
mcastu.c castmu() calls aggravate() for MCAST_AGGRAVATION (:826-830); js/mcastu.js emits the message then records recordMcastGap('wizard.c aggravate') at :773-777.
wizard.c intervene() calls aggravate() in result case 3 (:784-802) after the Wizard of Yendor is killed. No JavaScript intervene() implementation exists; this is a separate unported caller path.
dependencies: dungeon.c In_W_tower() returns the consumed hero/monster region predicate. js/dungeon.js already exports In_W_tower(x, y, level, state); compute the hero result once and compare it with each monster result in source order.

The C global fmon linked list maps to state.level.monlist. DEADMONSTER(mtmp) is the mhp < 1 check. Update each existing monster object in place: clear exactly STRAT_WAITFORU | STRAT_APPEARMSG, clear msleeping, and conditionally set mfrozen=0 and mcanmove=1.

rng.c rn2() supplies the consumed result only when mcanmove is false. js/wizard.js already imports rn2; use the call-site random stream where its caller supplies one. Calls to aggravate() discard its void result, so there is no return-valued dependency.

result.summary: The AD_SLEE dispatcher arm stops at a missing uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_slee() implementation during a landed monster attack against the hero. The whole source function has three attacker/defender branches; this case reaches its monster-to-hero branch, where C prints the hit message and its recorded rn2(5) value of 3 fails the effect gate. functions.name: mhitm_ad_slee
functions.sourceReview: Compared the complete uhitm.c:3478-3522 body. Hero-attacks-monster tests the sleeping flag, then magic cancellation, then rnd(10)/sleep_monst; successful sleep prints only when visible and runs slept_monst. Monster-attacks-hero awaits hitmsg before gm.multi, rn2(5), and verbose magic-cancellation checks; it updates M_SEEN_SLEEP on resistance, otherwise clears it, calls fall_asleep(-rnd(10), TRUE), and prints the blindness-sensitive message. Monster-versus-monster preserves the two sequential sleep_monst(mdef, rnd(10), -1) calls. A successful first call freezes the defender, so the second returns false; a failed first call short-circuits before the second draw. The later message, STRAT_WAITFORU clear, and slept_monst body are source-present but unreachable for the ordinary live movable defender covered here. No unsupported return substitutes remain in this function.

functions.name: mhitm_ad_conf

This orthogonal ICE destination reaches the common checks and hack.c:1253-1254 returns TRUE. hack.c:2843-2856 and 2873-2980 then move the hero and call spoteffects(TRUE).

The evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261001190602-v17.json records 33/34 screens and its sole missing screen is step 33; the preserved v17 queue identity is 1 remaining screen and 34 recorded steps. The failure label “test_move() door or special terrain movement” is emitted by the JS boundary helper at js/hack.js:1458-1461, not by the source test_move() result.

The earliest JS stop is cmd.js:executeMovement() calling preflightDomoveDestination() before movement intent at js/cmd.js:2723-2733. For an unoccupied, non-obstructed ICE destination, js/hack.js:1758-1759 calls requireSimpleHeroDestination(); its ordinaryDestination list at 1452-1457 omits ICE and throws. The owner’s comment at js/hack.js:5000-5011 explicitly says the spoteffects() caller gate excludes the ice-warning arm; upstream hack.c:3312-3462 is the whole source unit and includes that branch at 3402-3415 plus recursion state at 3314-3339. This makes hack.c:spoteffects() the actionable whole-function file-port scope, with existing domove_core and teleds callers preserved.

The later intended ray behavior remains a separate gap: the recording never selects the wished wand, so it is not evidence for zap.c:weffects() -> zap_over_floor() -> melt_ice(). Current js/zap.js:5162-5212 records that melt_ice() has no ported owner; do not infer that behavior from this case’s title.

result.summary: The remaining fire-ray screen is caused by the unported zap.c:melt_ice() call in zap_over_floor’s ZT_FIRE branch. When the ray reaches ice, C changes the tile to its underlying pool or moat (or clears DB_ICE on a drawbridge), performs the ice side effects and redraw, then reports “The ice crackles and melts.” JavaScript currently calls note_unported() at this source site, leaving the terrain and message unchanged. The first RNG mismatch at zap_over_floor:5186 is a later pool-evaporation draw, not a random call in melt_ice().

source.branch: When zap_over_floor handles ZT_FIRE on a square for which is_ice(x,y) is true: ordinary ICE changes to POOL or MOAT according to icedpool, while an ice-covered drawbridge clears DB_ICE. The helper stops the melt timer, applies trap/object/vision effects, redraws, reports the message when visible or underfoot, handles boulders, and runs hero or monster floor effects.
callers: zap.c:zap_over_floor at 5173-5174; reached by zap.c:dobuzz for each visible ray square. JS js/zap.js:5211-5213 currently records note_unported("zap.c melt_ice") instead of invoking the helper.
trap.c:dofiretrap at 4313; the hero fire-trap path. JS js/trap_effects.js:2178-2179 has the corresponding melt_ice note.
trap.c:trapeffect_fire_trap at 1812; the monster fire-trap path. JS js/trap_effects.js:2298-2299 has the corresponding melt_ice note.
eat.c:vomit at 3781; the acidic-form branch. JS js/eat.js:2032-2033 currently refuses the acidic-form arm before this ice check, so that production path remains separately unsupported.

zap.c:melt_ice_away at 5130; the timer callback. JS js/timeout.js:365 registers the callback without an implementation, and zap.c:start_melt_ice_timeout is also still an explicit JS gap in the cold-ray path.
dependencies: trap.c:trap_ice_effects(x,y,TRUE) is a void, state-changing callee and has no JS implementation. Its C body clears a trapped monster and converts or deletes eligible traps as ice melts (trap.c:7174-7193); retain a named note_unported("trap.c trap_ice_effects") gap only when a trap is present until that separate source function is ported.

boulder_hits_pool() returns a boolean consumed by melt_ice() to detect an impossible failed pool fill; js/do.js exports an async implementation at 677, so the caller must await and preserve that result.
minliquid(mtmp) is explicitly cast to void in C; js/mon.js has the async helper at 2210, so run its side effects but do not use its return value.
melt_ice() itself returns void. zap_over_floor() retains its separate rangemod return contract, consumed by dobuzz() to adjust ray range; do not use a melt_ice return as the range delta.

evidence: The immutable v17 evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261001190602-v17.json records this case at 33/34 screens, 2151/2158 RNG calls and 33/34 cursors; the only remaining screen is segment 0, step 33, key h. Its earliest reported RNG difference is C rnd(5)=2 at zap_over_floor(zap.c:5186), while the screen and cursor also differ.

The C recording challenges/cases/v17/wizard-fire-ray-melts-wished-ice-slot-o.session.json ends step 33 with “The ice crackles and melts. Some water evaporates.” The recorded animation frames show the fire beam crossing the wished ice and the tile changing from ice to liquid before the final pool evaporation message.

Upstream zap.c:5040-5079 defines the complete void melt_ice() body: default message; clear DB_ICE or restore the underlying POOL/MOAT and clear icedpool; stop MELT_ICE_AWAY; call trap_ice_effects, obj_ice_effects and unearth_objs; recalculate underwater vision; newsym before Norep; process boulders; then call spoteffects underfoot or minliquid for a monster in the pool.

Upstream zap.c:5141-5187 puts melt_ice() in the ZT_FIRE ice arm at 5173-5174. rnd(5) at 5186 belongs only to the following is_pool() arm. melt_ice() contains no direct random-number call, so the saved first RNG difference identifies later pool evaporation, not the source owner.

Upstream zap.c:dobuzz (4780 onward) paints and delays the beam at each square before calling zap_over_floor(), then re-reads the monster because melting ice can change its floor effects (zap.c:4828-4861). JS js/zap.js:5888-5912 follows the same animation-before-floor-effect order; call melt_ice at the existing note site without moving the call ahead of the beam frame or delay.

A direct upstream source search, rg -n "melt_ice\(" nethack-c/upstream/src/{zap.c,trap.c,eat.c}, finds zap.c:zap_over_floor and melt_ice_away, trap.c:dofiretrap and trapeffect_fire_trap, and eat.c:vomit, in addition to the definition. The paired rg search for melt_ice, zap_over_floor and trap_ice_effects in nethack-c/patches returns no matches; the owning behavior is the upstream C body.

The matching retainedCases context in .cache/C56-accepted-preparation-evidence.json attributes the C outcome to zap.c:weffects -> buzz -> zap_over_floor -> melt_ice, with ice becoming water. Direct inspection confirms that attribution: js/zap.js:5211-5213 still skips the C helper. The retained trace’s zap_over_floor:5186 RNG caller is downstream pool handling and must not be treated as melt_ice ownership.

functions.name: xname_flags
functions.sourceReview: Read the complete C objnam.c:xname_flags definition (581-1030) and its JS split, xname_flags (829-922) plus xnameBase (467-827). C reserves the PREFIX region in nextobuf, selects source actual/description/discovery names (including the Samurai override), applies stored-state observation and artifact-discovery effects, and routes personal names before the class switch. The switch covers every compiled object class, including slime-mold fruit singular/plural handling, the partly-eaten FOOD prefix before both glob and ordinary food formatting, statue species articles, and the one-shot next-boulder field update. It checks the byte-buffer bound before pluralization, appends game-over apparel/wrapper/motif disclosures, appends instance names, lowercases only the initial T in an artifact instance "The ", and returns the suffix pointer when the result starts with "the ". JS follows this order with xnameBase for class formatting and an immutable string plus byte bufferOffset for the C pointer result. This unit is impure: it can observe objects, clear known, set cleric BUC knowledge, discover artifacts, consume next_boulder, and, during game-over disclosure, call the impure apparel/motif formatters. The default invalid object-class arm formats the C numeric class and calls the discarded-void impossible helper; JS names note_unported('pline.c impossible') there, an invalid-state diagnostic gap outside ordinary valid object inputs.

C obtains greatest_erosion and returns the original buffer unchanged at zero; otherwise it computes strlen(buf) * erosion / (2 * MAX_ERODE), calls the void buffer mutator wipeout_text with o_id XOR unsigned ubirthday, then returns buf. JS returns the equivalent immutable string and sends the corresponding seed/state to engrave.js:wipeout_text. The branch can use core RNG when its seed is zero, including a seed that reaches zero during wipeout_text recurrence, so this helper is impure for valid eroded inputs. wipeout_text is a void effect dependency, not a return-value closure claim.

functions.name: block_door

C first checks the SHOPBASE room, IS_SHOP and current u.ushops, then requires the keeper to exist and be inside the shop. It returns TRUE with “blocks your way!” only when the keeper is at ESHK.shk (the keeper home coordinate), the target equals ESHK.shd (the shop door coordinate), the keeper is not helpless, and debit, billct or robbed is set. It otherwise returns FALSE. JS preserves this order. The function is impure because its true arm emits output; two complete recordings execute the false-return branch through the diagonal test_move caller. Their observed movement proves false return, but the frames do not identify which internal predicate made it false, and they do not claim the blocking-message branch.

evidence.entryPointReview: The 124 selected source units comprise hack.c:pooleffects/spoteffects and 122 required whole functions across the traced dependency closure. Each row records its complete C definition, canonical JavaScript implementation symbol, direct C-to-JavaScript production callers, source-derived purity, and either a result-pinning test or a full matching recording. All 82 pure rows have source-pinned tests; all 42 impure rows have at least one matching recording through a production caller. A bounded replay audit at b421d8f92badf87a42206e384bddfc62b2968233 confirmed 52/52 committed recordings match (201,697 RNG calls, 3,166 screens/cursors, 388 animation frames; no committed diagnostic mismatch). The later correction head a83e92eba9287bb896dddca3277eb8491a1e2ddc passed the seven affected focused suites and lint. Recorded entry paths cover ordinary movement onto wished ICE and a ZT_FIRE melt (admitted v17 ranges), recursive fire-trap melts over POOL and MOAT, cold-ray timer creation/restart and MELT_ICE_AWAY expiry, acid vomit from timeout and choking callers, same-square teleport arrival, wasinside xkilled/pickup, covetous master-lich relocation, DROWNING and BURNING rescue returns, object-name helpers through read/sortloot/bhito, positive liquid boulder handling through melt_ice and moverock_core, gas-region membership transitions, and diagonal movement into D_BROKEN shop doors. For block_door the strict records prove the helper ran and returned false; they do not show the true “blocks your way!” branch or reveal the hidden keeper predicates. For block_door, ESHK.shk stores the shopkeeper home position and ESHK.shd stores the door coordinate the helper may block. functions.name: fruitname

Its consumed helpers strstri (hacklib.c:740), makesingular (objnam.c:3037-3167), and nextobuf (objnam.c:142-149) have accepted whole-source evidence in GOALS.json under port-hack-pooleffects-spoteffects-recursive-ice-v17-20261002. result.summary: The first measured v21 mismatch occurs when C reaches weapon.c:dry_a_towel after apply.c:use_towel cleans the hero’s cream-blinded face with a carried wet towel. JavaScript records note_unported('apply.c dry_a_towel') and skips the void call, omitting the towel drying message and the wetness, wielded-state, and inventory updates. The smallest coherent source family is weapon.c:finish_towel_change, wet_a_towel, and dry_a_towel, wired at their existing source callers.

source.branch: finish_towel_change clamps changed towel wetness to 0–7, updates obj->spe, changes gu.unweapon when the hero wields the towel, and refreshes inventory for carried towels. wet_a_towel reports only an increase and dry_a_towel reports only a decrease; both finish any changed value through that helper. Feedback depends on verbose and whether the towel is carried or carried by a visible monster. This case reaches the dry branch with amt -1 after use_towel removes u.ucreamed; drying_feedback is true when the towel is uwep.
callers: apply.c:use_towel (four wet-towel cleanup branches; assigned case reaches the cream-cleanup branch)

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:use_towel (112–197), especially 173–187, removes u.ucreamed and then calls dry_a_towel(obj, -1, drying_feedback) when is_wet_towel(obj). functions.name: s_suffix
functions.sourceReview: Read the complete hacklib.c:s_suffix definition at 345-359. functions.name: ing_suffix
functions.sourceReview: Read the complete hacklib.c:ing_suffix definition at 363-396. It copies input into static buf, saves the end pointer, checks trailing " on", " off", and " with" in that exact case-insensitive order, saves the final-space suffix using strrchr, then applies the case-insensitive er no-op, CVC doubling with the exact vowel set aeiouwy, case-insensitive ie-to-y, and lowercase-e deletion in source order. functions.name: quest.lua
